source.publication: 2025 MI-1040 Forms and Instructions (includes Form 4884 instructions)
source.section: Form 4884 Section A lines 9-16 (PDF page 20 'Recipients born before 1946': private benefits up to 65,897 single; PDF page 21 Line 9, Line 16); Schedule 1 lines 14, 27, 28 (PDF page 14, PDF page 17); MI-1040 lines 9a, 10, 13-17 (PDF page 10 Line 9a, Line 10, Line 17; PDF page 11 example: line 14 income subject to tax less line 15 exemptions = line 16 taxable income)

worked: Federal AGI = private pension 50,000.00 + IRA distribution 30,000.00 + dividends 4,000.00 + taxable Social Security 30,600.00 = 114,600.00. Federal taxable income = 114,600.00 - federal standard deduction (15,750 + 1 x 2,000 age 65 or older = 17,750.00) = 96,850.00; given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored. Michigan (born 1939: Section A): line 9 limit 65,897.00; line 10 0.00; public 0.00; private benefits 50,000.00 + 30,000.00 = 80,000.00, over the limit, so the smaller, 65,897.00, goes to Schedule 1 line 27. Line 14 Social Security 30,600.00. Line 28: 14,688 - 65,897.00 < 0, so 0.00 (the dividends stay taxed). Subtractions 96,497.00. Line 14 = 114,600.00 - 96,497.00 = 18,103.00; exemption 5,800.00; line 16 = 12,303.00. MI-1040 line 17 tax = 12,303.00 x 0.0425 = 522.8775, to the cent 522.88 (the form, in whole dollars, gives 523). No credits; state income tax 522.88.
